question: What is the main difference between natural immunity and artificial immunity?

options.A: It requires synthetic vaccines to be effective
options.B: It relies entirely on pharmaceutical treatments
options.C: It develops without medical intervention or immunization
options.D: It only functions during the first week of life

explanation: Natural immunity happens through normal daily life exposures and natural body processes rather than through vaccines or medical treatments. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T9#BMP111_U6_T9_h1)

question: How does innate natural immunity compare to adaptive natural immunity?

options.A: Adaptive immunity is present fully formed before birth
options.B: Innate immunity requires previous exposure to a specific pathogen
options.C: Adaptive immunity offers no immunological memory for future infections
options.D: Innate immunity provides immediate, non-specific protection from birth

explanation: The innate system acts as the body's first line of defense, reacting to all germs in a general way without needing prior exposure. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T9#BMP111_U6_T9_h1)

question: Which cells create long-term memory in the immune system after a natural infection?
explanation: Memory cells stay in the body long after an infection clears, ready to recognize and fight off the same germ if it returns. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T9#BMP111_U6_T9_h2)

question: Why is active natural immunity called 'active'?

options.A: The body actively manufactures its own antibodies and immune cells
options.B: It involves receiving ready-made antibodies from another person
options.C: It requires physical activity and exercise to function properly
options.D: It only works when the heart pumps at a faster rate

explanation: Active immunity means the person's own body does the work of fighting the infection and producing protective cells and antibodies. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T9#BMP111_U6_T9_h2)

question: Which antibody class passes from the mother to the baby across the placenta during pregnancy?
explanation: IgG is the specific antibody type that can cross the human placenta to provide passive protection to the developing fetus. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T9#BMP111_U6_T9_h3)

question: A mother asks why exclusive breastfeeding helps protect her young baby from stomach bugs. What is the reason?

options.A: Breast milk kills all bacteria permanently so infections can never happen
options.B: Breast milk delivers maternal IgA antibodies directly to line the baby's gut
options.C: Breast milk replaces the need for any future childhood vaccinations
options.D: Breast milk forces the baby's bone marrow to create permanent memory cells

explanation: Secretory IgA in breast milk coats the infant's digestive tract, helping neutralize local germs safely. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T9#BMP111_U6_T9_h3)

question: What is the main job of antigen-presenting cells in natural immunity?

options.A: Pumping blood and oxygen throughout the lymphatic system
options.B: Engulfing pathogens and displaying their fragments to other immune cells
options.C: Producing red blood cells inside the bone marrow
options.D: Creating physical barriers like skin and mucous membranes

explanation: These cells capture invaders and show pieces of them to T-cells and B-cells to trigger a targeted defense. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T9#BMP111_U6_T9_h4)

question: What is the function of cytokines during an immune response?

options.A: They act as chemical messengers to stimulate other immune cells
options.B: They form a hard physical wall around the infected tissue
options.C: They transport oxygen molecules directly to lymphocytes
options.D: They dissolve the cell walls of beneficial bacteria

explanation: Cytokines are signaling proteins released by immune cells to coordinate the attack and manage the body's response. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T9#BMP111_U6_T9_h4)

question: Why can high levels of maternal antibodies in a newborn interfere with some early childhood vaccines?

options.A: The maternal antibodies may neutralize the vaccine antigens before the infant's immune system responds
options.B: The maternal antibodies cause permanent damage to the infant's bone marrow
options.C: The vaccine will cause the mother's own immune system to react violently
options.D: The infant's body will immediately excrete all vaccines through the digestive tract

explanation: Remaining maternal antibodies can attach to vaccine particles just like real germs, which stops the infant's own immune system from building a response. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T9#BMP111_U6_T9_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a safe way to build lasting immunity against dangerous childhood diseases?

options.B: Allowing the infant to consume nutrient-rich colostrum
options.C: Deliberately exposing a child to wild natural infections
options.D: Receiving protective antibodies via transplacental transfer

explanation: Intentionally exposing children to natural infections is unsafe because it risks severe complications and illness compared to standard immunizations. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T9#BMP111_U6_T9_h5)
